comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C5, C53-C56, C58-C60. Both evaluations agree that KLP-6 D458A mutation releases autoinhibition and increases microtubule binding but does not induce dimerization or processivity, distinguishing it from UNC-104. Both treat this as a key, well-supported finding.

Perfect alignment on claims C84-C86, C102. Both evaluations accept that L640F mutation prevents dimerization and correlates with reduced in vivo transport, validating CC2's physiological importance. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect alignment on claims C111-C114. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental evidence for additional KLP-6 activation factors, while peer reviewers accept this as reasonable speculation. Both acknowledge these are untested hypotheses about future directions.

Strong alignment on claims C3, C47-C50 (OpenEval) vs C3, C48-C50 (peer). Both agree that artificially dimerized KLP-6(1-390)LZ exhibits processivity, demonstrating dimerization requirement. Both treat the data as well-supported without concerns.

Strong alignment on claims C4, C61-C67, C70-C73. Both evaluations strongly support that E412K mutation induces UNC-104 dimerization and processivity. Peer review includes additional claims C88-C89, C105 addressing concentration-dependent equilibrium and microtubule substrate effects. Both treat this as a central, compelling finding.

Partial alignment on claims C31-C32. Both agree KLP-6 full-length is monomeric by SEC and mass photometry. OpenEval additionally includes C37 (microtubule binding without processivity), while peer review includes C2 (background context). Both fully support the monomeric characterization.

Strong alignment on claims C6, C75-C78 regarding CC2 coiled-coil domain's role in dimerization. Peer review R5 encompasses broader scope including deletion experiments (C79-C80, C82-C83) and functional implications (C94, C98-C101) that OpenEval addresses in separate results R7, R18, R19. Both strongly support CC2's critical role.

Partial alignment on claims C79-C80, C82-C83. OpenEval focuses specifically on CC2 deletion preventing dimerization even with E412K mutation. Peer R5 groups this with broader CC2 findings. Both evaluations support the data without concerns.

Strong alignment on claims C38-C40, C44 regarding tail-domain microtubule binding. Peer R6 additionally includes C37, C42-C43 about KLP-6's binding behavior and lack of processivity. Both evaluations treat the tail-domain binding site identification as solid experimental evidence.

Strong alignment on claims C69, C103-C104 regarding microtubule substrate differences (brain microtubules vs axonemes). Both accept this as important methodological finding explaining discrepancies with prior work. OpenEval notes speculation about PTMs (C103) lacks direct testing, while peer reviewers accept it as technical consideration.

Partial alignment on claims C106-C108. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the dimerization-before-cargo model lacks direct in vivo evidence. Peer reviewers accept the revised model as reasonable interpretation. OpenEval is more cautious about speculative aspects, while peer review treats it as valuable contribution.

Minimal overlap on claim C110. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting PIP2 speculation lacks experimental support. Peer R9 groups this with broader model acceptance (C106-C110). OpenEval explicitly flags lack of lipid/membrane experiments, while peer review accepts speculation.

Minimal overlap on claim C109. OpenEval notes this cites prior in vivo work (Niwa et al., 2016) validating E412K effects. Peer R9 includes this in broader model acceptance. Both treat the citation as appropriate supporting evidence.

Minimal overlap on claims C88-C89 regarding concentration-dependent monomer-dimer equilibrium. OpenEval addresses this separately as interpretation of SEC vs mass photometry differences. Peer R3 groups with E412K dimerization findings. Both support the equilibrium model.

Minimal overlap on claim C43. OpenEval separately notes lack of processivity for non-dimerized constructs. Peer R6 includes this with broader KLP-6 characterization. Both accept the data without concerns.

Minimal overlap on claims C94, C98 regarding CC2's role across kinesin-3 family. OpenEval addresses literature synthesis separately (C90-C98). Peer R5 focuses on experimental CC2 data. Both support CC2's fundamental importance for dimerization.

Minimal overlap on claims C99-C101 regarding CC2's physiological importance. OpenEval addresses functional implications separately from structural findings. Peer R5 groups with broader CC2 characterization. Both support the conclusions.

OpenEval identifies potential typographical error in claims C33-C36 regarding gliding velocities (nm/s vs μm/s discrepancy). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific concern about the ~3000-fold difference in reported values.

OpenEval separately evaluates gliding assay data (C45-C46, C57) showing motor domain retains activity regardless of autoinhibition. No corresponding focused peer review evaluation, though data not questioned elsewhere.

OpenEval separately notes claim C74 showing KLP-6(E409K) remains monomeric, confirming mechanistic differences from UNC-104 are not mutation-site dependent. No corresponding focused peer review evaluation.
OpenEval separately evaluates background/context claims C1, C7-C18 as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background claims.
OpenEval separately evaluates prior work summary claims C19-C30 as appropriately cited motivation. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate literature review claims.
OpenEval separately evaluates rationale claims C51-C52 for comparing KLP-6 and UNC-104 constructs. No corresponding focused peer review evaluation.
